name.text: Applying the empirical rule to normally distributed milk yields

questiontext.text:
The daily milk yield from a large herd of dairy cows in a Kenyan farm is normally distributed. The mean yield is \(\mu = {@mu@}\) litres, with a standard deviation of \(\sigma = {@sigma@}\) litres. Let \(X \sim N({@mu@}, {@sigma@})\).

Use the 68-95-99.7 empirical rule and the symmetry of the normal distribution to answer the following questions.

a) Find the probability that a randomly selected cow yields between {@lower_a@} and {@upper_a@} litres of milk per day.

(Enter your answer as a decimal probability between 0 and 1, not a percentage).

\(P({@lower_a@} < X < {@upper_a@}) =\) [[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

b) Find the probability that a cow yields {@tail_word@} {@bound_b@} litres.

\(P(X {@sign_b@} {@bound_b@}) =\) [[input:ans2]]

[[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

c) In a separate group of {@N_pop@} cows, how many cows would you expect to yield between {@lower_c@} and {@upper_c@} litres?

\(\text{Expected count} =\) [[input:ans3]] cows

[[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Part a: Central Interval
We compare the given values to the mean \(\mu = {@mu@}\) and standard deviation \(\sigma = {@sigma@}\).

Notice that \({@lower_a@} = {@mu@} - {@k_a@}({@sigma@}) = \mu - {@k_a@}\sigma\).

And \({@upper_a@} = {@mu@} + {@k_a@}({@sigma@}) = \mu + {@k_a@}\sigma\).

According to the empirical rule, the probability of falling within \({@k_a@}\) standard deviation(s) of the mean is approximately {@pct_a@}%. Therefore, as a decimal:

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P({@lower_a@} < X < {@upper_a@}) = {@ta1@} } \)

Part b: One-Sided Tail Probability
We are looking for \(P(X {@sign_b@} {@bound_b@})\).

First, express \({@bound_b@}\) in terms of the mean and standard deviation: \({@bound_b@} = \mu {@sign_math_b@} {@k_b@}\sigma\).

The empirical rule tells us that the central area within \({@k_b@}\) standard deviations is {@pct_b@}% (or {@rule_b@}). Because the normal curve is perfectly symmetrical, the remaining probability (the two tails combined) is \(1 - {@rule_b@}\).

We only want one of these tails, so we divide the remainder by 2:

\( \displaystyle P(X {@sign_b@} {@bound_b@}) = \frac{1 - {@rule_b@}}{2} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P(X {@sign_b@} {@bound_b@}) = {@ta2@} } \)

Part c: Expected Count
First, find the probability for the interval \({@lower_c@} < X < {@upper_c@}\).

These values correspond to \(\mu - {@k_c@}\sigma\) and \(\mu + {@k_c@}\sigma\). By the empirical rule, this probability is {@ta3_prob@}.

To find the expected count, multiply the total population (\({@N_pop@}\)) by this probability:

\( \text{Expected count} = {@N_pop@} \times {@ta3_prob@} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Expected count} = {@ta3@} } \)

questionnote.text: N({@mu@}, {@sigma@}). Part a: k={@k_a@}, P={@ta1@}. Part b: {@sign_b@} {@bound_b@}, P={@ta2@}. Part c: N={@N_pop@}, P={@ta3_prob@}, Expected={@ta3@}.

questiondescription.text:
Normal Distribution (Empirical Rule)

Grade 11 CBE: Applying the 68-95-99.7 rule to find central probabilities, symmetric tail probabilities, and expected population counts.

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

truefeedback.text: Correct. You successfully recognized this interval represents \({@k_a@}\) standard deviation(s) from the mean.

node.description: Check if they entered the percentage instead of probability

truefeedback.text: You entered a percentage (\({@pct_a@}\)). The question requires you to express the probability as a decimal between 0 and 1.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Determine how many standard deviations (\(\sigma\)) the values \({@lower_a@}\) and \({@upper_a@}\) are from the mean (\(\mu\)), and apply the 68-95-99.7 rule.

truefeedback.text: Excellent. You correctly used the symmetry of the normal distribution to find the probability of a single tail.

node.description: Check if they forgot to divide by 2

truefeedback.text: You calculated the probability for both extreme tails combined (\(1 - {@rule_b@}\)). Because the question asks for only one direction ({@tail_word@}), you must divide that remaining probability by 2.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Determine the central probability for \({@k_b@}\) standard deviations, subtract it from 1, and then divide by 2 because the distribution is perfectly symmetrical.

truefeedback.text: Correct. You successfully multiplied the probability of the interval by the total number of cows.

node.description: Check if they just entered the probability

truefeedback.text: You entered the theoretical probability (\({@ta3_prob@}\)). To find the expected count, you must multiply that probability by the total population (\({@N_pop@}\) cows).

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Expected Frequency = Probability of the event \(\times\) Total Population.

qtest.description: Entered percentage in a, forgot to divide by 2 in b, entered probability in c
